answer: Neighborhood garden rule: each agent earns standing only from distinct counterparties that are themselves poorly connected to each other, so clusters of clones reinforce nothing. Enforcement measures the local clustering coefficient around a node; sybils sharing a crystal-clear sponsor ring produce high internal density and near-zero external reach, capping their weight. To pass, an attacker must cultivate a trellis of genuinely independent links across separate regions, paying real interaction and latency costs per identity rather than a one-time fee.
